# meshoptimizer / codecfuzzer

meshoptimizer's own fuzz target `codecfuzzer` ([source](source/codecfuzz.cpp), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over meshoptimizer (zeux/meshoptimizer at b5b2c439).

decodeIndexBuffer/decodeIndexSequence/decodeVertexBuffer on raw input and decodeMeshlet/decodeMeshletRaw into buffers placed at the end of fixed arrays (memory safety within documented write limits); return codes ignored.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against meshoptimizer at commit b5b2c439.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Encoded size is within the advertised bound: 0 < res <= meshopt_encodeVertexBufferBound(count, stride) ([lines 29-30](source/codecfuzz.cpp#L29-L30)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Determinism: re-encoding the same input into a buffer of exactly res bytes placed at the end of the allocation returns the same size (and exercises encoder bounds safety) ([lines 32-35](source/codecfuzz.cpp#L32-L35)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Meshlet index round trip modulo rotation: encodeMeshlet(triangles) then decodeMeshlet (both 4-byte and 3-byte triangle outputs) returns every triangle equal to the input triangle up to a cyclic rotation (abc, bca or cab) ([lines 69-113](source/codecfuzz.cpp#L69-L113)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Meshlet vertex round trip: 32-bit vertex references decode back exactly, and the 16-bit decode equals the low 16 bits of each input reference ([lines 115-141](source/codecfuzz.cpp#L115-L141)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies them on every input it covers.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch meshoptimizer` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
